title: Extension Tag Validity Period under Title & Registration Services
content:
An extension tag's base validity, in calendar days counted from its issue date, is the larger of the service's extension tag validity days and the validity of the order's original tag, which is the calendar days from the original tag's issue date to the expiration printed on it. An extension tag under Title & Registration Services is never issued for longer than twice the validity of the order's original tag, and its validity is a whole number of days.

## Inputs and records

| Input | Record |
|---|---|
| the original tag's issue date | the temporary tag entry with sequence number 1 on the title order: its issue date |
| the expiration printed on the original tag | the same entry: its printed expiration date |
| the service type's extension tag validity days | the extension tag validity figure of the order's service type |

The validity of the original tag is counted in calendar days from its issue date to its printed expiration date. The ceiling is twice that count.

## Worked examples (hypothetical orders, each under a service type whose extension tag validity is 30 days)

1. Original tag issued 1 March, printed expiration 30 April: original validity 60 days. The larger of 30 and 60 is 60, the ceiling is 120, so the extension tag is valid 60 days.
2. Original tag issued 1 March, printed expiration 31 March: original validity 30 days. The larger of 30 and 30 is 30, the ceiling is 60, so the extension tag is valid 30 days.
3. Original tag issued 1 March, printed expiration 11 March: original validity 10 days. The larger of 30 and 10 is 30, but the ceiling is 20, so the extension tag is valid 20 days.

## Reading the ceiling

The ceiling is fixed by the original tag alone: a later extension tag already on the vehicle does not change it.
